verdict.why: Option X implements the brief more completely and buildably. It covers all three items of the request: per-persona configurations with a closed vocabulary and panel/report gate checks (R1–R11), stand-capture reuse with an explicit manifest contract sent to the stand (R14, D14–D18), and agent-tester untouched (R15) — plus the answer on the board with backlog rows and dates, exactly as the brief demands. Every requirement has a planted-fixture acceptance check, contradictions are resolved (config-only findings must be backed by a differing reference, R8), and edge cases like config_gap, partial panels, and back-compat (R12) are all decided with reasons. Option Y is coherent and lighter, but it leaves the stand path blocked on unknowns (Q5, Q6), pushes phase-2 questions to the stand, lets panel config use a looser locale regex, and its config_only 'control' check is weaker than X's refutation rule against zero-edge rows.
risks: X invents rules the brief does not state (max two edge values per persona, at least two zero-edge personas, waiver line) — reasonable but strictly beyond the brief
X's Row B depends on the stand publishing a capture manifest that task-pipeline does not control; the due date may slip
X's web pseudo-double via injected script is synthetic and may produce false findings; spec acknowledges this
X's scope is large for size M; the test-first plan mitigates but the surface (gate, agent doc, doctrine, tests, board traffic) is heavy
